slides.text: As a professional assassin, my biggest occupational flaw is my crippling social anxiety. I broke into my target's apartment at 2 AM, dressed in tactical black, holding a silenced pistol. I knocked over a lamp. The target, a terrifyingly large mob boss, bolted upright in bed. 'Who's there?' he yelled. Out of pure reflex, I squeaked, 'Room service?' I don't know why I said that. He lives in a townhouse.

Miraculously, he bought it. 'Bring the cart up, I'm starving,' he grumbled, turning on the bedside light. I couldn't just shoot him now; it felt incredibly rude. So, I went to his kitchen and made him a grilled cheese sandwich. I meticulously cut the crusts off, my gun tucked awkwardly under my arm. I brought it to him on a silver tray I found in the hallway.

He took one bite and started crying. 'My mother used to cut the crusts off exactly like this,' he sobbed, hugging my terrifying, heavily armed torso. 'I’m changing my life. I’m leaving the mob forever.' He handed me a duffel bag of cash and walked out the front door in his pajamas. I stood there holding a half-eaten sandwich, wondering if I should bill my client for culinary services.
